stakeholder.stakeholder_description: Fictional service technician who commissions the item and services it in the workshop. Trained to the documented procedure and to nothing else.

need_statement: The item shall publish its state, its limits and its fault condition to the vehicle manufacturer's control unit, and shall act on that control unit's state requests only when doing so is consistent with the item's own safety evaluation.
rationale: The vehicle manufacturer owns the vehicle-level safety case and needs enough of the item's state to integrate with it, and needs the item not to become a hazard to that case through an unhandled request. The two halves are in tension: an item that ignores requests cannot support vehicle features, and an item that honours them can be steered into a state its own monitoring has already judged unsafe. The need resolves the tension in one direction only - the item's own evaluation wins - and that direction is a deliberate asymmetry, not a neutral one.

priority.rationale: The vehicle manufacturer owns the vehicle-level safety case and needs enough of the item's state to integrate with it, and needs the item not to become a hazard to that case through an unhandled request.

limitation: Declared, not elicited. The corpus has no interface agreement with any vehicle manufacturer, so the set of requests the item may honour and the set it may refuse is not written down anywhere. The 'won't be able to talk the item out of a safety decision' half of this need is asserted by the cybersecurity requirements, not demonstrated.
